reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes Baked Beans as a BNB deposit-and-reward miner through a website and referral link. It presents unusually high returns, including an advertised 8% daily return and 2920% APR, while encouraging viewer participation and highlighting a 12% referral reward. Although it includes a disclaimer and does not establish actual losses or successful withdrawals, the video itself promotes this high-return crypto participation flow.

opening.argument: The material repeatedly qualifies itself as opinion and risk information rather than a promise. The description says the information is informational only, identifies the speaker as unlicensed, warns of considerable loss risk, and tells viewers to conduct their own research. It also expressly says no particular outcome is guaranteed. Those are direct, prominent limitations on how viewers should interpret the discussion, supporting non-scam financial commentary rather than deceptive certification of a result.

citations.quote: The information contained in this video is for informational purposes only. Nothing said in
the speaker who is not a licensed financial advisor or registered investment advisor
Trading cryptocurrencies & NFT's poses considerable risk of loss
The speaker does not guarantee any particular outcome & you should do your own research & risk assessment

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution emphasizes return language but underplays the accompanying qualifications. The same description says the speaker is not an adviser, warns of loss, disclaims guaranteed outcomes, and directs viewers to research and assess risk. A high stated return may be worth scrutiny, but these disclosures do not establish that viewers were deceptively promised payment or that the speaker certified the project as safe.

citations.quote: The speaker does not guarantee any particular outcome & you should do your own research & risk assessment
Trading cryptocurrencies & NFT's poses considerable risk of loss

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A disclaimer cannot erase the video’s affirmative promotion. The speaker personally says he invested, describes the deposit-and-reward mechanism, and calls the return guaranteed. Those statements are materially stronger than a neutral risk notice, while the disclaimer itself admits the speaker is not qualified to validate the opportunity.

opening.argument: The speaker presents a hands-on explanation of how the tool operates, openly acknowledging limited knowledge and intending a fuller follow-up. He explains the distinction between compounding and taking rewards, demonstrates entering values into a spreadsheet, and uses a contract calculator to derive an expected figure. That is a personal demonstration and tutorial-style walkthrough, with the viewer invited to research independently, rather than evidence that the creator is certifying an investment outcome.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution’s selected investment phrases describe what the demonstration is teaching, not what the creator claims to have independently verified. The speaker says he is still learning and plans a fuller video, while the spreadsheet labels the result as expected daily rewards. A tutorial can explain a speculative tool without becoming a fraudulent guarantee.

citations.quote: I'm still learning but just showing you guys the next project that I've jumped into
this is not accurate but it's your expected daily rewards in bnb

true_side_reply.rebuttal: This is not merely abstract education: the walkthrough tells viewers how to deposit BNB, compound, take rewards, and follow a six-to-one strategy. The speaker also says he invested and encourages viewers who want to get into it to use the referral link. Calling it a demonstration does not remove its practical solicitation.

opening.argument: The supplied material more specifically shows a branded rewards interface with ordinary project terms and an optional referral promotion. The frames display a rewards balance, rebake and eat-beans controls, a stated developer fee, and a referral link; the description candidly says affiliate links generate a kickback. Nothing supplied shows a credential request, a downline-income structure, failed withdrawals, or an actual loss. The evidence therefore supports a disclosed crypto promotion and referral arrangement, not proof of a scam mechanism.

citations.quote: (We Get A Kickback From These Affiliate Links)

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats the existence of a deposit-and-reward interface as dispositive, but that only identifies the product being discussed. The supplied record does not establish that the contract failed to pay, that credentials were solicited, or that viewers were recruited into a downline. The referral is disclosed as a kickback, and the speaker frames participation as optional help.

citations.quote: (We Get A Kickback From These Affiliate Links)
if you guys wanna get into this and you wanna help me out, you can

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing evidence does not make the promotion ordinary. The video expressly connects depositing BNB to rewards, reports a personal return, advertises an 8% daily rate, and provides a referral path. A scam classification can rest on promoting an implausibly high-return participation flow; it does not require proof of a credential request, withdrawal failure, or realized victim loss.
